== Overview ==
{{spoiler|book=lh-04-the-pilot|[[The Iron]] [[Legion]] is a pervasive and aggressive force characterized by its fusion of biological matter and mechanical technology. Their fleet consists of ships that are part machine and part living tissue, often created by seizing existing vessels and infecting them with organic material. This combination results in a collection of gruesome, mismatched trophies that nevertheless operate with high levels of mechanical coordination. The [[Legion]] functions like a virus or disease, spreading through systems by consuming both organic and mechanical matter to replicate itself. They utilize underground factories known as [[Scourge Warrens]] to facilitate this expansion and maintain [[Iron Hives]]. While their individual ships may lack the quality of advanced vessels like those belonging to [[the Advocates]], they rely on overwhelming numbers to achieve their goals. The [[Legion]]'s primary drive is an imperative to incorporate everything into its own collective. Without a central [[Authority|authority]], the group acts mindlessly, focused on devouring and replicating to ensure their own propagation. However, they can be directed by an [[Iron King]], a powerful leader who is a masterwork of flesh and [[steel]]. While the [[Legion]]'s behavior can appear chaotic, an [[Iron King]] provides organized direction and seeks to claim significant assets, such as ships, for the [[Legion]]'s use. The group has been known to aggressively target [[Galactic Union]] territory, occasionally abandoning other regions to focus their efforts on the [[Union]]. Despite their reputation as villains that no one supports, some have expressed interest in potentially repurposing the [[Legion]]'s manufacturing and expansion capabilities for other ends.}}

== The Captain ==
{{spoiler|book=lh-01-the-captain|[[The Iron]] [[Legion]] is an enemy military force composed of a swarm of abominations, including [[Reavers]] and [[Pawns]], created by fusing machines with living beings. Operating from [[Hives]] and utilizing specialized technology like hunter-ships, [[Penetrators]], and thousand-yard battleships made of metal and flesh, they emerge from [[Subspace]] to aggressively push into [[Galactic Union]] territory. Although the [[destruction]] of their King a year ago left them leaderless and mindlessly devouring to propagate, they have recently demonstrated a unity suggesting the guidance of a King. This endless force seeks to make everything part of the [[Legion]], causing significant damage to [[The Last Horizon]] and conquering numerous planets. Consequently, various figures such as [[Varic Vallenar]] and the crew have engaged in a crusade to dismantle and destroy them.}}

== The Engineer ==
{{spoiler|book=lh-02-the-engineer|Following the recent [[destruction]] of their [[Grand Hive]], the [[Iron]] [[Legion]] remains a priority concern for the [[High Council of the Advocates]]. This group, which was once fought by [[Starhammer]] during his conquest, utilizes [[Bishop of the Iron Legion|Bishops]] capable of deploying various biological and magical attacks such as viruses, acid mists, and mental pulses. During their military engagements, the [[Legion]] has cut through Jak's system fleet and deployed a hundred thousand [[Pawns]], even facing down the full force of [[The Last Horizon]]. Their capabilities include turning Contrasaurs into Behemoths and maintaining a [[Hive]] that resembles a moon at night. Because they possess the potential to outnumber the narrator's forces, [[Sola Kalter|Sola]] was brought on to handle them, and they have also been fought by [[Varic Vallenar|Varic]]'s crew.}}

== The Knight ==
{{spoiler|book=lh-03-the-knight|Spanning across the galaxy, the [[Iron]] [[Legion]] is a group of straightforward villains that spreads like a virus without regard for witnesses. Engaged in conflict with the [[Karoshan|Karoshans]], they were responsible for an ambush that resulted in [[Kyri Prest]] losing her arm. Though they were eventually cleared from the [[Lesser Karoshan system]], a hunt was placed upon them, and they faced combat against both the narrator and [[Raion Raithe|Raion]]'s crew. While their power is comparable to a threat from [[Neth’terith]]'s swarm, the [[D’Niss]] utilize different tactics to combat them. The group also manufactures new weapons and was summoned by [[Starhammer]] for the purpose of creating an [[Iron King]].}}

== The Pilot ==
{{spoiler|book=lh-04-the-pilot|[[The Iron]] [[Legion]] is an entity that creates objects from twisted [[steel]] and [[Iron|iron]], and it has been engaged in ongoing conflicts with the [[Galactic Union]] for centuries. Speculation exists that [[The Last Horizon]] may be conquering planets to serve them, while certain worlds report experiencing withdrawals. Evidence of their presence includes the use of their technology in biological remains, shipments of their components aboard the Vallenar, and the existence of experimental subjects. Because the landmass of Fathom resembles a victim of their actions, [[Sola Kalter|Sola]] has utilized contacts to track their movements and performed mercenary missions to stop them. While the [[Fallen Sword]] is dedicated to their [[destruction]], the [[Legion]] remains ready to serve.}}

== Notable quotes ==
* {{spoiler|book=lh-01-the-captain|“Now let’s get the Iron Legion off us,” I said.<ref name="lh-01-the-captain-c16" />}}
* {{spoiler|book=lh-01-the-captain|“We have an Iron Legion battleship over our heads. Now’s the time.”<ref name="lh-01-the-captain-c16" />}}
* {{spoiler|book=lh-01-the-captain|“We intend to wipe out the Iron Legion,” I said.<ref name="lh-01-the-captain-c19" />}}
* {{spoiler|book=lh-01-the-captain|“Contact me if you have trouble with the Iron Legion.”<ref name="lh-01-the-captain-c21" />}}
* {{spoiler|book=lh-01-the-captain|“The Legion can attack almost anywhere, if they send a single Hive on a suicide mission.<ref name="lh-01-the-captain-c36" />}}
